report:
## Conclusion: No — ivermectin does **not** lower the risk of death in COVID-19

The best available evidence from large, well-conducted randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews shows that ivermectin does **not** reduce mortality or meaningfully improve clinical outcomes in COVID-19 patients.

### Key evidence

1. **PRINCIPLE trial (NEJM, 2022):** A large double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT found that early treatment with ivermectin did not reduce hospitalization or prolonged emergency department observation among outpatients with COVID-19. A follow-up analysis concluded ivermectin is "unlikely to provide clinically meaningful improvement in recovery, hospital admissions, or longer-term outcomes."
   — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869

2. **TOGETHER trial (Brazil, 2022):** A platform trial of ~3,515 patients found no significant benefit from ivermectin for preventing hospitalization or extended emergency observation.
   — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic

3. **Systematic review & meta-analysis (BMC Infectious Diseases, 2022):** A rigorous synthesis of RCTs concluded that ivermectin did not significantly improve critical outcomes including mortality, ICU admissions, or ventilator use.
   — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12879-022-07589-8

4. **Updated meta-analysis (Annals of Medicine and Surgery, 2025):** Confirmed that although ivermectin may alleviate some symptoms, it did not significantly improve mortality, ICU admissions, or ventilator use.
   — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40110299/

### Why earlier studies suggested benefit

Early small studies and some meta-analyses (often including low-quality or retracted trials) reported apparent mortality reductions. However, when large, high-quality RCTs were conducted, these benefits disappeared. Major health authorities — the FDA, WHO, and IDSA — all recommend **against** ivermectin for COVID-19 outside of clinical trials.

**Bottom line:** The current high-quality evidence does not support ivermectin as a treatment that reduces death from COVID-19.
